rationale: Review of the second-scenario direct check 5a560c55 (unit-claim-install-snapshot-alignment), whose fresh execution b9d811ad439049be9c19247ec7db97b2 completed the comparison with the declarative prerequisite matched, comparison_complete and witness_complete true, and the assertion violated: after the install retained a tail (node_last_index 5, term 1, tail_retained true), the AppendEntries a leader sends next - anchored at the snapshot index - was rejected (append_success false, tail_replaced false, last entry unchanged). This is a second violated scenario of the same requirement and a sharper one than the first: the misalignment does not only misreport the last entry, it stops the follower accepting the leader's entries. This review supplies the required checker_correspondence item and re-resolves the claim-level applicability issue, which is open again for this artifact because a resolution answers its own lineage.

review_items.rationale: Requirement versus encoded predicate: the obligation requires the receiver to align its log with the installed snapshot so its last entry does not come from an unconfirmed branch, and this scenario encodes the operational consequence of getting that wrong - the AppendEntries a leader sends after a successful install (nextIndex = snapshot index + 1, hence anchored at the snapshot index) must be accepted. S57 shows the receive path adopting the snapshot index and compacting without setting the last log, S58 shows the compaction removes entries through the snapshot index, S54 shows the effective last entry is the maximum of log and snapshot position so the anchor is no longer the last entry once a tail survives, and S8 shows that the previous-log check then falls through to the log store and rejects with NoRetryBackoff. Entry and caller duties: the harness declares the retained tail from the install event, anchors the request at the installed index with a conflicting term, and delivers it through the production handler. Identity: op_id tail-1 appears on both the install event and the append event, and the prerequisite correlation matched. Oracle: acceptance and the resulting last entry are read from emitted fields, not tests_passed; the run exited 0 while the anchor was rejected, which is the case this oracle must catch. Observation path and completion: the install response and the append response were both received, and the run completed. Counterevidence: none of the open issues is evidence against the encoded predicate; the protocol-alignment reading and the adaptations are recorded below.
limitations: The retained-tail state was seeded through the caller-owned log store rather than produced by a real leader's snapshot decision, so reachability under a leader remains a premise.

Node goroutines were disabled and a substitute answered restore futures; the check isolates the two handlers' decisions and does not exercise FSM restore, the main loop or the leader's subsequent nextIndex walk.
The check reports the receiver's rejection only: whether the leader then decrements nextIndex and re-sends a snapshot (and how long that loop lasts) was not measured.

conf.TrailingLogs was 0 so compaction ran at the snapshot index; with the default the trailing-log guard would have skipped compaction entirely and the anchor would have remained in the log, which is a different starting state and is not covered here.

review_items.rationale: The antecedent is declared before the result: the install event reports the retained tail from the handler's own bookkeeping, and the appended request is anchored at the installed index, which is the position a leader uses after a successful install. Nothing was filtered by the observed rejection, and no applicability condition depends on append_success. The claim-level condition concerns whether a later AppendEntries is an acceptable substitute for aligning at install time, which is the reading the claim addresses rather than a precondition for whether the requirement applies to this receiver.
limitations: One carrier, one installed index and one tail shape; other index/tail combinations are not covered.
Real-leader reachability and the leader's follow-up behaviour remain open.

condition_dispositions.rationale: Whether relying on the next AppendEntries is acceptable in every deployment is a separate question from whether the receiver owes alignment at install time; the second scenario measures the consequence of that reliance but does not depend on how it is characterised, and the boundary is carried in this review's limitations.

resolutions.rationale: This is the claim-level record of the snapshot-protocol conflict, open again here because a resolution answers the artifact it was written against. The answer is the same attributed reading, now sharpened by a second executed scenario: the protocol requires a receiver that cannot confirm the snapshot's last included entry to discard the log, the implementation leaves that removal to a later AppendEntries (S57, S58), and the second scenario shows why the deferral matters - with a retained tail the anchor index is no longer the effective last entry (S54), so the very AppendEntries that was supposed to perform the removal is rejected (S8) and the tail survives. The claim therefore asserts the install-time alignment duty, and the question of whether the deferral is nevertheless harmless in a deployment is retained as an outer boundary.
scope_limitations: Whether a real leader drives a follower into the retained-tail state, and how long the resulting rejection lasts, remain open outside this claim.
